Chapter Details: Status of digitalisation of records in rural facilities
Definition: The status of digital data capture in rural primary healthcare clinics
Comments: Rural primary healthcare clinics in Republic of the Congo (COG) predominantly use paper-based systems for patient records, registers, and prescriptions. DHIS2 implementation was announced in 2019 by the Ministry of Health, but as of 2020-2021 assessments, no evidence of completion or facility-level digital recording exists; national HMIS relies on aggregate data entry, likely from paper reports at district level GHS Index report. No electronic health records in use (score 0 in 2020 assessment). World Bank health projects support DHIS2 nationally with tablets for verification, but no mention of rural clinic-level digital patient data capture World Bank Health Sector Project. WHO notes limited eHealth; francophone African rural clinics typically rely on paper 'registres' and 'cartes de patient', with central digitization. No recent (2024-2026) evidence of shift to digital at rural level; score 1 as paper is standard without rural-specific digital pilots.

revision_notes: Fetched all three originally cited sources. The 2020 World Bank ICR for the Congo Health Sector Project confirms DHIS2/tablet use for aggregate reporting and verification above facility level only, and the 2021 GHS Index Congo-Brazzaville profile confirms no electronic health records in use. Fresh searches for 2024-2026 evidence of rural clinic-level digitisation in Congo-Brazzaville found none; digital-health programmes located (IMA World Health DHIS2 scale-up, RTI eIDSR pilot) concern the Democratic Republic of Congo, a different country, and were excluded as not applicable. Score of 1 (Entirely paper) confirmed.
revised_comments: Rural primary healthcare clinics in the Republic of Congo continue to rely on entirely paper-based systems for patient records, registers and prescriptions at the facility level. The 2020 World Bank Implementation Completion Report for the Congo Health Sector Project confirms that DHIS2 support, including tablets, is used for aggregate reporting and verification at higher administrative levels but does not extend to facility-level electronic patient records in rural clinics. The 2021 Global Health Security Index country profile for Congo-Brazzaville likewise finds no electronic health record systems in use. No evidence of a shift to facility-level digital data capture in rural clinics has been identified.

Definition: The status of digital data capture in rural civil registry offices
Comments: Rural civil registration offices (centres d'état civil) in the Republic of the Congo predominantly use paper-based birth registers. No evidence found of operational electronic CRVS systems in rural areas. A national digital system, SIFEC (Système Intégré des Faits d'État Civil), was validated in February 2026 but remains in implementation phase, with no confirmed rural rollout. WHO reports functional civil registration (75-94% completeness) nationally but lacking vital statistics; rural completeness likely lower per World Bank/UNICEF surveys, though specific figures unavailable. Births declared at local offices within 30 days.

revision_notes: The originally cited World Bank rural birth-registration indicator and PMC article do not speak to facility-level digitisation and were superseded by fresher, more authoritative official sources. Two Ministry of Finance government articles and an ACSI (Agence Congolaise des Systemes d'Information) release, all dated 18-20 February 2026, confirm SIFEC completed its technical validation workshop but remains at the recommendation-validation stage pre-deployment, with participants explicitly requesting the human, material and financial resources needed to deploy it. No rural civil registry office is using it. Score of 1 (Entirely paper) confirmed and updated to the February 2026 evidence.
revised_comments: Rural civil registration offices in the Republic of Congo continue to record births, deaths and marriages on paper. The national digital civil registration platform, the Systeme Integre des Faits d'Etat Civil (SIFEC), developed by the Agence Congolaise des Systemes d'Information, completed a technical validation workshop in Brazzaville on 18-20 February 2026, but as of that date remains at the recommendation-validation stage, with participants calling for the human, material and financial resources needed for deployment. No rural rollout has occurred, so civil registration remains entirely paper-based at the facility level.

Definition: The status of digital data capture in rural primary schools
Comments: Republic of the Congo is developing an integrated EMIS as part of the GPE-funded TRESOR project (2024), including national strategy, legal framework, platform operationalization, yearbooks, and dashboards. Republic participates in AU/GPE KIX EMIS workshops (2024). UNESCO notes efforts to digitize primary education after prior EMIS non-functionality. No evidence of digital recording at rural primary school level (attendance, enrollment, grades); data collection likely paper-based at schools with aggregation/digital entry at higher levels. Fits "predominantly paper with some digital (pilots, donor projects, or aggregate reporting)."

revision_notes: The original comments concluded the row 'fits predominantly paper with some digital', which would correspond to code 2, yet the recorded Value Code was 1. The metadata guidance restricts this variable to facility-level data capture, excluding higher-level aggregation or dashboards. On that stricter facility-level test, no evidence of digital data capture in rural primary schools was found: the GPE TRESOR programme document and independent technical assessment (2024) describe a legal framework for EMIS only established in November 2023 and a strategy still under development, with data reliant on centrally compiled, donor-financed school directories rather than facility-level digital capture; the AU-IPED workshop of May 2026 confirms EMIS modernisation is still at the assessment stage. Score of 1 (Entirely paper) confirmed as correct for the facility level; the 'predominantly paper with some digital' framing in the prior comments referred to aggregate-level reporting, which is out of scope for this variable.
revised_comments: Data capture in rural primary schools in the Republic of Congo remains paper-based at the facility level, with attendance, enrolment and grades recorded in paper registers. The government is developing an integrated Education Management Information System (EMIS) under the GPE-financed TRESOR programme, with the legal framework for the system only established in November 2023 (Decree No. 2023-1751) and the comprehensive EMIS strategy still under development. An independent technical assessment describes the enabling environment for education data as weak and fragile, relying heavily on donor-financed, centrally compiled school directories (annuaires scolaires) rather than facility-level digital capture. In May 2026 the African Union's Pan-African Institute for Education for Development held a workshop in Brazzaville to help the country assess and modernise its EMIS, confirming that digitisation of facility-level data capture, including in rural schools, has not yet occurred.

Definition: The status of digital data capture in rural police stations
Comments: Extensive searches across web, academic papers, US State Department 2023 HR report, UNODC, and targeted queries for Congo-Brazzaville (Republic of the Congo) rural police stations yielded no specific evidence on how rural police record criminal cases or complaints. Reports highlight police abuses, corruption, and poor conditions in stations (mostly urban), but no mentions of digital case management, EMIS-like systems, or even paper vs. digital practices in rural areas. Congo's low development, poor rural infrastructure, and lack of documented reforms suggest paper-based if any, but genuinely no evidence found. Score 0: unknown.

revision_notes: Re-checked all three originally cited sources plus fresh searches; none describe recordkeeping practices in rural police stations specifically. The State Department 2023 Human Rights Report and Afrobarometer material address corruption and public trust, not digitisation. An older (2016/2017) State Department report indicates the penitentiary system relied on non-computerised recordkeeping despite computer equipment being available in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire, an urban, not rural, data point. A tertiary AI-aggregated source (Grokipedia) referencing a 2025 gendarmerie reorganisation law and a planned 'unified incident-reporting platform' was found but is not a primary or sufficiently authoritative source per our evidentiary standard and was not used to change the score. Unknown (0) confirmed: genuinely no evidence available on rural police station recordkeeping.
revised_comments: No authoritative evidence has been identified on how rural police stations in the Republic of Congo record cases or complaints, or on whether registers are paper-based or digital. Available reporting, including the US State Department's 2023 Human Rights Report and Afrobarometer surveys, addresses police corruption, abuse and public trust but does not describe recordkeeping practices, while earlier reporting on the penitentiary system indicates continued reliance on non-computerised recordkeeping in urban facilities despite the availability of computer equipment. No facility-level information specific to rural police stations is available.
